headline: US Technegas revenue up 74% year-on-year post FDA approval; active commercial sites doubled from 35 to 70; targeting ~2,000 of 5,200 lung-imaging locations for a $180M pulmonary embolism market, with growth beyond PE in COPD, asthma and pulmonary hypertension
reasoning: Following FDA approval in late 2024 and full reimbursement clearance, Cyclopharm deployed a full US sales force and has seen 74% year-on-year Technegas revenue growth, doubling active commercial sites from 35 to 70. A landmark international consensus guideline — encompassing the Society of Nuclear Medicine, American College of Nuclear Medicine, European Association of Nuclear Medicine, and Australia New Zealand Society of Nuclear Medicine — named Technegas the agent of choice, further accelerating the US pipeline. The company estimates about 5,200 US locations image the lung in a way that could use Technegas, with approximately 2,000 centres expected to represent the vast majority of the target market, implying a $180 million opportunity in pulmonary embolism alone. The broader FDA-approved indication extends to COPD, asthma, and pulmonary hypertension, which management views as the real long-term growth driver beyond PE. The sales force ramp was deliberately measured rather than aggressive, with selective rollout to understand key delivery points before accelerating.
quote: We entered there after an approval, yeah, at the end of of 24 we have full reimbursement. So that took a little bit of time to get underway. At the end of last year, we we deployed a full sales force and I think importantly one of the biggest milestones ever... an international guideline that encompassed the US, the Society of Nuclear Medicine, the American College of Nuclear Medicine, the European Association of Nuclear Medicine, and the Australia New Zealand Society of Nuclear Medicine came out with a consensus guideline. First time ever that anything like that to that scale has ever been published. And it again, like the Chinese, what was done in parallel named technicas as the agent of choice. We've already seen, you know, an uptick in engagement in the in the US, We already had a very strong pipeline, but we're seeing acceleration in in those discussions right now... There's, there's about 5200 locations in the US that are, are imaging the lung the way that they, they could use tech and gas... We expect that about two thousand of those centres are going to give us the the vast majority of the of the of the market in which we're targeting and that we expect that to be 180 million just in diagnosing pulmonary embolism.
episode_title: Cyclopharm sees major China growth opportunity

headline: China's seven medical bodies unanimously named Technegas gold standard for lung ventilation imaging, relegating DTPA to backup, with 1,200+ nuclear medicine departments and plans to double — 160 systems installed so far, significant expansion ahead
reasoning: Seven Chinese medical bodies led by the Chinese Thoracic Society issued a consensus recommendation naming Technegas as the preferred ventilation agent for lung imaging with 100% consensus, explicitly calling it the gold standard. This relegates the competing product DTPA — currently the dominant agent in China — to a purely backup role. Cyclopharm has been in China for over two decades and currently has about 160 systems installed. China is planning to double the number of nuclear medicine cameras and departments (from 1,200+) over five years in a state-backed expansion, which aligns directly with Cyclopharm's growth ambitions. The company expects to replicate the ~85% market share it holds in comparable international markets. The recommendation also covers indications beyond pulmonary embolism, including pulmonary hypertension, expanding the addressable market.
quote: Andrea, this is a you know, I, I was just only here a few months ago talking about another set of international guidelines. This is, this is exceptional in the fact that it's multidisciplinary. So it was led by the Chinese Thoracic Society, seven other medical bodies along with their nuclear medicine colleagues recommending 1010 key points in how to diagnose pulmonary embolism. And the number one recommendation, as you kindly put at 100% consensus, was naming Technicas as the agent of choice... So relegating cheaper generic alternatives to purely a backup. The other alternative is, is a product called DTPA. It's a product that we compete with in other markets outside of the the US. You know we hold about a 85% market share in in this type of procedure when we entered the US 80, that 85%, we expect that to occur in China.
episode_title: Cyclopharm sees major China growth opportunity

headline: Cyclopharm CEO acknowledges share price disconnect from operational momentum, attributing it to thin trading and pointing to continued US delivery as the key re-rating catalyst.
reasoning: Despite strong operational metrics — record revenue, doubling of US installations, peak cash burn passed, and 90%+ consumable margins — the share price has not responded in kind. The CEO attributes this partly to the stock being thinly traded. He believes the market is not pricing in the full opportunity and that continued execution in the US will be the turning point. Institutional shareholders are described as supportive, and the company is focused on delivering on its US strategy as the primary value driver.
quote: Every indicator that we've just talked about, it's kind of going the other way from what you see on the share price, I think, you know, we're thinly traded share. And you know, my focus is is just delivering on the US. And I suppose that's going to be the turning point for us.
episode_title: The Aussie small cap betting big on the US

headline: Cyclopharm CEO highlights record first-half 2026 revenue driven by accelerating US installations of Technegas, with margins above 90% on consumables and a long runway to 2,000 target sites.
reasoning: Cyclopharm reported record first-half 2026 revenue of $17.5 million, up 14%, with US revenue up 74% year-on-year. Installations of its radioactive diagnostic agent Technegas in the US doubled from 35 to 70 at the half and reached 83 by the time of reporting, against a target market of approximately 2,000 sites out of more than 5,100 doing these procedures. Consumable gross margins exceed 90% and are expected to expand further as the US business scales. Newly released US nuclear medicine clinical practice guidelines are seen as a game-changer and a key commercial tool, given there is no comparable product in the marketplace. The company operates in 67 countries and holds approximately 85% market share in established markets, with a similar outcome expected in the US over time. Cash burn has already peaked, with the business now moving toward sustained margin expansion.
quote: That's certainly the foundation but across the board Andrew all of the things that you know, we've been working on, um, have delivered the growth. You're right. 17.5 up, uh, up 14% US up 74%... at the half last year, we were at 35 installations at the, at the half, uh, this year were at 70. And even at the time of the report, we were at 83. So we've seen that acceleration. And one of the things that that not even baked into that number yet is the guidelines. I think last time I was here talking about the the nuclear medicine guidelines that were just released in the US, we believe that is a game changer for us.
episode_title: The Aussie small cap betting big on the US

headline: Cyclopharm CEO highlights accelerating US growth as first 11-site hospital deal signals enterprise-scale adoption of Technegas lung imaging agent
reasoning: Cyclopharm has signed its first double-digit, all-at-once installation deal with University Hospitals across 11 US sites, marking a step-change from the typical one-or-two-site test-and-grow model seen at Massachusetts General, Stanford, and Emory. The US business model is lease-based rather than capital-sale, reducing customer capex barriers and accelerating rollout while generating high-margin consumable annuity revenues. US revenues grew 73% in the latest half, from ~$1.1m to over $2m, and revenue-generating installations rose from 50 at the AGM to 70 by end of July. Upcoming US clinical guidelines are expected to name Technegas as the agent of choice, reinforcing its already globally recognised clinical positioning across 67 countries. McBrayer also flagged AI as a future growth vector, given the rich functional lung data the product generates, with clinical trials underway with multiple partners.
quote: University Hospitals is our first double digit all at once in in the installation deal. Usually what we see is one of the sites will will come on board at 1 or 2 locations and then grow from there. We've seen that at Massachusetts General Stanford. Uh, Emory, this is our first example of, uh, instead of test driving it, they've bought a whole fleet for the family... our consumables are certainly in the US are a very high margin business. Every time we do an installation that that revenue starts dropping to the bottom line... the US went from about, you know, 1.1 million to just over two, $2 million. So we've had 73% increase in in the US.
episode_title: Cyclopharm's US growth story gathers pace
